In addition to typical histological changes of PBC, patients with PBC + NCPF showed features consistent with OPV (Figures 2D–F), including luminal narrowing, sclerosis, or disappearance of the portal vein branches. Portal fibrosis was more evident in the PBC + NCPF group compared to the PBC-only group

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). B: Elastica-Masson-stained liver needle-biopsy core at 100× from the same PBC patient; the caption states extended fibrosis is not seen, a specific histological feature supporting early-stage (Scheuer Stage II) PBC. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Liver biopsy hematoxylin-eosin panel from a patient with primary biliary cholangitis, showing portal tracts expanded by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration; supportive histologic manifestation of PBC. B: Classic PBC histology: chronic inflammation with granuloma in the portal tract causing bile duct injury, consistent with a florid duct lesion. C: CK19 immunohistochemistry showing ductular proliferation in a liver biopsy from a patient with PBC; ductular reaction is a recognized cholestatic histologic feature but less specific than florid duct lesion. D: Liver biopsy hematoxylin-eosin panel showing a non-caseating granuloma within the lobule in a patient with PBC; granulomas are a recognized but less common PBC histologic finding.

The caption explicitly documents bilateral scleral icterus and xanthelasmas on the medial side of bilateral lower eyelids (marked by arrows), and the in-text physical examination confirms these findings in the PBC patient. Xanthelasma is a recognized cholestatic hyperlipidemia-associated manifestation of PBC. The scleral icterus is visible in the image and stated in the caption but is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is listed as a proposed finding. No third-party copyright is indicated; the caption states direct written consent was obtained.
